answer: Proof-of-throughput-over-time resists sybils: an identity must sustain a measured rate of verifiable work across a window, not a single burst, so a fake cannot flash one computation and idle. Like yarrow spreading steadily, genuine throughput must persist from dawn to dusk of the window; a farm splitting one machine across many identities cannot sustain the per-head rate simultaneously. The fable of cheap mass participation fails because sustained throughput per identity is hardware-bound and cannot be faked by bursting then going quiet.
